title: Idempotency, exactly-once effects and crash recovery
subtitle: A restart never repeats a provider call, a broker restart never re-runs work the GPUs hold, and an agent's claimed completion is a claim.
lede: The rule I apply in every system below is simple to state. I design for the crash window explicitly and decide, per system, whether a duplicate or a gap is the worse failure. FAFOHive lets agents use a payments provider, an email/CRM provider and social-publishing providers through a governed gateway. A repeated payment or a second marketing email is a real-world harm, so I made the gateway account for every call durably, and a restart does not repeat a provider call. The gateway's design is in Agents with real tools and no keys. In my own social modules a duplicate public post is worse than a missing one.
quote: An outcome I cannot confirm gets reconciled by reading, never retried by sending again, and work is done when its result has been acknowledged.
evidence: Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: intent and budget committed before any provider call, and uncertain outcomes resolved by a read and never by a resend.
Idempotency key design: keys bound to request inputs, so a replay returns the saved receipt and a replay with changed inputs is refused.
Distributed systems correctness: a broker that counts work done only when acknowledged, and agent launches bound to an authorised claim so a replay returns the existing job.
author: Corey James
